summary: Sées is a mid-sized Norman Gothic cathedral built mostly between about 1210 and 1310, with a six-bay nave, an ambulatory choir and two west towers. It is the only Norman Gothic cathedral without a crossing tower. Weak foundations left the nave leaning, which prompted repeated reinforcement from the 16th century through the 19th, and the choir was largely rebuilt after 1869.

phases.what: Romanesque cathedral rebuilt after the 1048 fire, begun by Bishop Yves de Bellême, consecrated 1126
Construction of most of the present Gothic cathedral starts around 1210, with the foundations skimped for lack of money
Choir, radiating chapels and transept built from the third quarter of the 13th century to the early 14th
An epitaph credits Jean de Bernières as the builder during this period
Cathedral consecrated by Bishop Philippe Le Boulenger on 27 September
Consolidation shortens the nave by one bay and adds two buttresses to the west front (16th century)
Brousseau builds a double buttress on the fourth north bay against the lean of the nave
Nave buttresses rebuilt, north side 1832-1838 and south side 1844-1850; the south tower spire rebuilt to match the north
Choir dismantled and rebuilt with foundations up to 8 m deep under Ruprich-Robert, finished by Petitgrand

events.what: Fire set during Bishop Yves de Bellême's siege of the cathedral destroyed much of the building.
Another fire during the wars between Henry II and Louis VII.
Hundred Years' War damage, with more in 1375.
Cathedral reconsecrated after profanation and repair.
Bishop Lallement closes the building because of its poor condition.
Joseph Brousseau starts restoration (to 1797), including removal of the crossing tower threatened by collapse.
Alavoine encases the west front in a heavy supporting frame with cast-iron colonnettes and pinnacles.
Ruprich-Robert appointed to direct the restoration; south transept done 1856, north transept begun 1869.
